help.intro: One whole day, twelve gaps, everything from this module at once: the accusative (einen Kaffee, den Bus), kein and keine, modal verbs with their infinitive at the end, and separable verbs with the prefix already waiting at the end of the sentence. Each gap has a hint — the verb and the person (aufstehen · ich) or the meaning and the noun (a (der Kaffee)) — and the job is to decide the form. Read the whole text first, because the end of a sentence (… auf, … an, … fern, … einkaufen) tells you what kind of verb the gap holds. This is the kind of text you will soon write yourself — a message, a diary entry, an answer to 'Wie war dein Tag?' — seen from the inside.
help.tips[0].title: Only masculine moves in the accusative
help.tips[0].text: einen Kaffee, einen Apfel, den Bus — but eine Banane, ein Brot. Look at the gender in the hint, then decide whether anything changes.
help.tips[0].examples[0].en: In the supermarket I buy a loaf, a banana and an apple.
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: At eight I take the bus to work, because I don't have a car.
help.tips[0].check.q: Zum Frühstück esse ich ____ Ei. (das Ei)
help.tips[0].check.why: Ei is neuter, and only masculine nouns change in the accusative, so it stays ein.
help.tips[1].title: The prefix is already at the end — type only the stem
help.tips[1].text: 'Ich ____ um sieben Uhr auf' wants stehe. The auf is there; your job is the conjugated half.
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: I get up at seven. In the evening I watch TV.
help.tips[1].trap: typing 'aufstehe' into the gap doubles the prefix. The two halves live at opposite ends.
help.tips[1].check.q: Am Morgen ____ ich das Fenster auf. (aufmachen · ich)
help.tips[1].check.why: The auf is already at the end of the sentence, so the gap takes only the conjugated stem: mache.
help.tips[2].title: A modal in the gap means an infinitive at the end
help.tips[2].text: 'Am Nachmittag ____ ich einkaufen' — the infinitive einkaufen at the end tells you the gap is a modal: muss.
help.tips[2].examples[0].en: In the afternoon I have to go shopping.
help.tips[2].examples[1].en: I want to watch a film, but I am very tired.
help.tips[2].check.q: Heute ____ ich lange arbeiten. (I have to work late today.)
help.tips[2].check.why: The infinitive arbeiten at the end means the gap is a modal, and 'have to' is müssen: ich muss.
help.tips[3].title: kein, not nicht, for an ein-noun or a bare noun
help.tips[3].text: Ich habe kein Auto — Auto would take ein, so its negation is kein. Milch has no article at all (Ich brauche Milch), so its negation is keine Milch.
help.tips[3].examples[0].en: At eight I take the bus to work, because I don't have a car.
help.tips[3].examples[1].en: I need milk too, but I can't find any milk.
help.tips[3].check.q: Ich trinke Tee, denn ich habe ____ Kaffee. (der Kaffee — Ich habe Kaffee.)
help.tips[3].check.why: Kaffee here has no article, so it is negated with kein; as a masculine object it becomes keinen.
help.remember[0]: Read the end of the sentence first: an infinitive means a modal in the gap, a prefix means a separable verb.
help.remember[1]: A der-noun as the object? Then -en: einen, den, keinen.
help.hook: Follow one ordinary day in German and fill in the small forms that hold it together: einen Kaffee, stehe … auf, muss einkaufen.
passageTranslation: I get up at seven o'clock and drink a coffee. At eight I take the bus to work, because I don't have a car. In the afternoon I have to go shopping. At the supermarket I buy a loaf of bread, a banana and an apple. I need milk too, but I can't find any milk. Then I call my sister. In the evening I watch TV. I want to watch a film, but I am very tired.
inlineBlanks[0].why: aufstehen is separable: the verb (stehe) goes second, auf goes to the end: Ich stehe um sieben Uhr auf.
inlineBlanks[1].why: Kaffee is masculine and the object of trinke (accusative), so ein becomes einen: einen Kaffee.
inlineBlanks[2].why: Bus is masculine and the object of nehme (accusative), so der becomes den: den Bus.
inlineBlanks[3].why: Auto is neuter and the object of habe. Neuter kein has no ending in the accusative: kein Auto.
inlineBlanks[4].why: müssen is irregular: ich muss (no ending). The other verb, einkaufen, goes to the end.
inlineBlanks[5].why: Brot is neuter, object of kaufe. Neuter ein stays ein in the accusative: ein Brot.
inlineBlanks[6].why: Banane is feminine, object of kaufe. Feminine stays eine in the accusative: eine Banane.
inlineBlanks[7].why: Apfel is masculine, object of kaufe (accusative), so ein becomes einen: einen Apfel.
inlineBlanks[8].why: Use kein (not nicht) to say 'no' before a noun. Milch is feminine, so: keine Milch.
inlineBlanks[9].why: anrufen is separable: rufe goes second, an goes to the end: Dann rufe ich meine Schwester an.
inlineBlanks[10].why: fernsehen is separable and irregular (du siehst), but with ich it is sehe; fern goes to the end.
inlineBlanks[11].why: wollen is irregular: ich will (no ending). The second verb, sehen, goes to the end.
